tasks.topic_en: Monotonicity and limit of a sequence
tasks.summary_pl: Ciąg $a_n=\frac{5n+6}{10(n+1)}$: granica i kresy (lim + a + b)
tasks.summary_en: Sequence $a_n=\frac{5n+6}{10(n+1)}$: limit and bounds (lim + a + b)
tasks.statement_en:
The sequence $(a_n)$ is given by $a_n=\frac{5n+6}{10(n+1)}$ for every natural number $n\ge1$.
a) Examine the monotonicity of the sequence $(a_n)$.
b) Calculate $\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n$.
c) Give the greatest number a and the smallest number b such that the condition $a\le a_n\le b$ holds for every n.
tasks.notes: part a) (monotonicity) is qualitative/excluded; value sums part b)'s limit (1/2) and part c)'s a (1/2) and b (11/20); text/key not OCR'd cleanly (garbled 2005-formula PDF), verified by rendering key PDF and by direct computation [verified: ok: Decreasing, lim 1/2, a=inf=1/2, b=a_1=11/20; summary states lim+a+b = 31/20. Matches key.]
part a) is a sketch (drawing); part b) asks for the solution set of an inequality, an infinite union of intervals

tasks.summary_en: Drivers A,B,C: late 5%,20%,50%; drive 2,2,1 times a week. P(late)?
tasks.statement_en: Students commuting to school observed that the bus being late depends on which of three drivers is driving. Statistical research showed that when driver A drives, the bus is late on 5% of trips, when driver B drives on 20% of trips, and when driver C drives on 50% of trips. During a 5-day school week, driver A drives twice, driver B drives twice, and driver C drives once. Calculate the probability that the school bus is late on a randomly chosen school day.

tasks.summary_pl: Trójkąt: $BC=400$m, kąty dane; oblicz $AB$ (zaokr. do 1 m)
tasks.summary_en: Triangle: $BC=400$m, angles given; find $AB$ (rounded to 1 m)
tasks.statement_en: Objects A and B lie on two sides of a lake. Field measurements of the relevant angles were made: [Figure: triangle ABC with angle ABC = 130 deg at B and angle ACB = 30 deg at C]. The distance between objects B and C equals 400 m. Calculate the straight-line distance between objects A and B, rounding the result to the nearest meter.
tasks.notes: verified against the crop image: angle at B = 130 deg, angle at C = 30 deg, so angle at A = 20 deg; AB = 400*sin(30)/sin(20) ~= 585 m

tasks.summary_en: Trapezoid circumscribed on a circle, $CS:SB=2:5$: find $\cos\angle CBD$
tasks.statement_en:
An isosceles trapezoid $ABCD$ with longer base $AB$ and shorter base $CD$ is circumscribed about a circle of radius $r$. The point of tangency $S$ divides the leg $BC$ so that $\frac{|CS|}{|SB|}=\frac{2}{5}$.
a) Find the length of the leg of this trapezoid.
b) Calculate $\cos\angle CBD$.
tasks.notes: part a)'s leg length is expressed in terms of the general radius r (symbolic, excluded); part b)'s cosine is r-independent, a genuine number, verified by direct recomputation
